A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SCULPT and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Matching relocated and renumbered content supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original GPT-4o and Llama 3.1 experiments, method ablations, perturbation tests and computational measurements, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original benchmark experiments and adds short-prompt tasks, summarization results and additional perturbation evaluations.

M1.justification: For summarization, v3 explicitly extends SCULPT's Critic inputs with evaluation scores such as ROUGE-L and cosine similarity, enabling graded feedback. The underlying prompt tree, reflection aggregation, Actor actions and search procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds short-prompt Object Counting, Odd One Out and Reddit sentiment classification, plus CNN/DailyMail summarization. It also adds grammatical corruption and French/Japanese token-noise scenarios within the retained classification tasks, substantially broadening evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: APEX appears in v2's perturbation comparison, Table 4, but is omitted from v3's corresponding Table 6. The cost comparison adds OPRO, and the new summarization experiment explicitly adapts ProTeGi to receive metric scores. The original main benchmark comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a summarization evaluation using ROUGE-1/2/L, MiniLM cosine similarity and a reported harmonic-mean aggregate. New perturbation protocols replace 20% of prompt tokens with French or Japanese, corrupt 20% of words, or corrupt the entire prompt. These substantially extend the evaluation design; previously documented benchmark splits, models, temperatures and search budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The robustness study expands from localized/global semantic perturbations to six conditions covering semantic, grammatical and multilingual noise on Causal Judgment and Misinformation. The cost analysis changes from Formal Fallacy with two methods to two tasks with three methods. Existing aggregation/rephrasing ablations, optimization-step analyses and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe averaging the top four prompts across three trials and retain the same standard-deviation reporting for the original benchmark comparisons. v3 introduces no new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedure; its added tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and appendix scores remain unchanged. New results include short-task averages of 85.43 for SCULPT versus 80.23 for ProTeGi, and summarization HM scores of 36.76 versus 35.92 (v3 Tables 4–5). Table 6 adds perturbation results and removes APEX entries. Formal Fallacy cost results are replaced by Causal Judgment/Misinformation measurements, which concern different tasks rather than same-setting cost improvements.

T1.justification: The prompt-tree definitions, optimization objective, update equations and UCB selection mathematics are retained, including the appendix algorithm. The added experiments introduce no new theoretical assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about hierarchical long-prompt optimization, robustness, information preservation and efficiency. The additional experiments broaden support without revising these central statements.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning short-prompt and generative applicability, recovery from grammatical and multilingual noise, and cost tradeoffs with OPRO. It newly identifies the Critic's ability to communicate graded output quality to the Actor as a limitation requiring further work. The standalone Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, and discloses OPRO's use of its top ten prior prompts. The replacement cost analysis no longer supplies the earlier Formal Fallacy LLM-call counts. Existing templates and core implementation settings are retained; the added tasks receive no corresponding appendix split or sample-size details.

R1.justification: The related-work section and reference list are unchanged. The paper retains its positioning around structured refinement of long prompts and the same novelty rationale relative to earlier optimization approaches.

P1.justification: Section 5 gains focused experimental discussions and a rewritten robustness passage. Computational analysis moves from a separate appendix section into the main results with revised content, and appendix references are updated. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds short-task and summarization tables, restructures the robustness table into task-specific blocks, and replaces the appendix cost table with a main-text table. Appendix tables are rearranged. All eleven figures retain their graphics, and the overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: The added short-prompt, summarization and broader perturbation experiments provide useful evidence for applicability beyond the original evaluation, while the code-access statement improves reproducibility information. The gain is limited by missing task-specific splits, sample sizes and uncertainty for the new tasks. Removing APEX's robustness results and the earlier Formal Fallacy call-count analysis also sacrifices some comparison detail.
